facts.statement: Geosaurus lived from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous periods.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous (Tithonian to Valanginian),

facts.statement: The genus Geosaurus was established by Georges Cuvier in 1824.
facts.quote: authority: Cuvier, 1824

facts.statement: Geosaurus is classified as an extinct marine crocodyliform in the family Metriorhynchidae.
facts.quote: Geosaurus is an extinct genus of marine crocodyliform within the family Metriorhynchidae

facts.statement: Geosaurus was a carnivore that likely spent its entire life in the ocean.
facts.quote: Geosaurus was a carnivore that spent much, if not all, its life out at sea.

facts.statement: No eggs or nests of Geosaurus have been found, leaving its lifecycle largely unknown.
facts.quote: No Geosaurus eggs or nests have been discovered, so little is known of the reptile's lifecycle

facts.statement: The type species of Geosaurus reached lengths of about 2.5 to 3 meters.
facts.quote: the type species was about 2.5 - 3 m long.

facts.statement: The type species Geosaurus giganteus is known from Late Jurassic deposits in Western Europe, specifically Germany.
facts.quote: The type species Geosaurus giganteus, meaning "giant Earth lizard", is known from Western Europe (Germany) of the Late Jurassic (Early Tithonian).

facts.statement: Geosaurus lapparenti is known from the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian) period in south-east France.
facts.quote: Geosaurus lapparenti is known from south-east France and dates to the early Cretaceous period (Valanginian).

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses starting in 2005 suggested that the genus Geosaurus is not monophyletic.
facts.quote: phylogenetic analyses begun in 2005 did not support the monophyly of Geosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that niche partitioning allowed multiple species of crocodyliforms to coexist in the same environment.
facts.quote: It has been hypothesised that niche partitioning enabled several species of crocodyliforms to co-exist.

facts.statement: Geosaurus giganteus and Dakosaurus maximus were likely the top predators in their ecosystem, characterized by large size, short snouts, and serrated teeth.
facts.quote: The top predators of this Formation appear to be G. giganteus and D. maximus, which were large, short-snouted species with serrated teeth.

facts.statement: Geosaurus belonged to the Crurotarsi group, which is the evolutionary lineage leading to modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Geosaurus was a large marine reptile of the group Crurotarsi, the line leading to modern crocodilians.

facts.statement: The modern Chinese term for Geosaurus is Dilong, meaning "earth dragon".
facts.quote: Como curiosidad, el término chino moderno para Geosaurus es Dilong 地龍 "dragón de tierra" (地龙 en chino simplificado)

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses starting in 2005 did not support Geosaurus as a monophyletic group.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, análisis filogenéticos iniciados en 2005 no apoyaron la monofilia de Geosaurus.

facts.statement: A revised classification presented by Young and Andrade in 2009 was used to list valid species.
facts.quote: Las especies incluidas abajo siguen la clasificación revisada, presentada por Young y Andrade en 2009.

facts.statement: The type species Geosaurus giganteus, meaning "giant land lizard", is known from western Europe (Germany) in the Late Jurassic (early Tithonian).
facts.quote: La especie tipo Geosaurus giganteus, que significa "lagarto de tierra gigante", es conocida de Europa occidental (Alemania), en el Jurásico superior (principios del Titoniense).

facts.statement: It was originally named Lacerta gigantea by von Sömmerring.
facts.quote: Originalmente se le llamó Lacerta gigantea por von Sömmerring.

facts.statement: Geosaurus grandis, originally described by Wagner in 1858, was formerly considered a species of Cricosaurus.
facts.quote: Geosaurus grandis, descrito originalmente por Wagner en 1858, fue antiguamente considerado una especie de Cricosaurus.

facts.statement: It is known from a complete skull.
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir de un cráneo completo.

facts.statement: Geosaurus lapparenti is known from southeastern France and dates to the early Cretaceous (Valanginian).
facts.quote: Geosaurus lapparenti es conocido del sureste de Francia y data de principios del período Cretácico (Valanginiense).

facts.statement: It was originally classified as a species of Dakosaurus.
facts.quote: Fue clasificado originalmente como una especie de Dakosaurus.

facts.statement: A large, undescribed species of Geosaurus is known from a single tooth from Plattenkalk in Germany.
facts.quote: Una especie grande y aún no descrita de Geosaurus es conocida a partir de un único diente de Plattenkalk en Alemania.

facts.statement: In 2009, Young and de Andrade published a redescription of Geosaurus examining the relationships and validity of species grouped in the genus.
facts.quote: En 2009, Young y de Andrade publicaron una redescripción de Geosaurus, examinando las relaciones y la validez de especies agrupadas en el género.

facts.statement: They found that several species previously classified in Geosaurus, including G. suevicus, G. saltillense, G. vignaudi, and G. araucanensis, were actually species of the closely related genus Cricosaurus.
facts.quote: Específicamente, ellos encontraron que varias especies antes clasificadas en Geosaurus, incluyendo G. suevicus, G. saltillense, G. vignaudi, y G. araucanensis eran realmente especies del género cercano Cricosaurus.

facts.statement: Rhacheosaurus gracilis, another long-snouted species, was also considered a species of Geosaurus (G. gracilis).
facts.quote: Rhacheosaurus gracilis, otra especie de hocico largo, también era considerada una especie de Geosaurus (G. gracilis).

facts.statement: Geosaurus carpenteri, also referred to as Dakosaurus at the time, is known from a partial skull.
facts.quote: Geosaurus carpenteri, también referida en su tiempo a Dakosaurus, es conocido de un cráneo parcial.

facts.statement: Teeth identical to those known from this species have been recovered from Yorkshire, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Dientes idénticos a los conocidos de esta especie han sido recuperados de Yorkshire, Reino Unido.

facts.statement: It was later assigned its own genus, Torvoneustes, by Andrade et al. in 2010.
facts.quote: Más tarde se le asignó su propio género, Torvoneustes por Andrade et al., 2010.

facts.statement: An unnamed specimen of Geosaurus was found in Oxfordian rocks in Cuba, though later studies showed this species was more closely related to Cricosaurus.
facts.quote: Un espécimen no nombrado de Geosaurus fue encontrado en rocas del periodo Oxfordiense de Cuba, aunque estudios posteriores han mostrado que esta especie estaba más bien relacionada con Cricosaurus.

facts.statement: Several species of metriorhynchids are known from the Mörnsheim Formation (Solnhofen Limestone, early Tithonian) in Bavaria, Germany.
facts.quote: Varias especies de metrirrínquidos son conocidas de la formación Mörnsheim (en la Caliza de Solnhofen, principios del Titoniano) de Baviera, Alemania.

facts.statement: Alongside Dakosaurus maximus, three species of Geosaurus are known, including G. giganteus, G. suevicus, and G. gracilis.
facts.quote: Junto a Dakosaurus maximus, se conocen tres especies de Geosaurus, incluyendo a G. giganteus, G. suevicus y G. gracilis.

facts.statement: It has been hypothesized that this niche differentiation allowed several species of crocodiliforms to coexist.
facts.quote: Se ha hipotetizado que esta diferenciación en nichos permitía a varias especies de crocodiliformes coexistir.

facts.statement: Dakosaurus and G. giganteus appear to have been the main predators in this area, possessing large serrated teeth in a short-snouted skull, contrasting with Cricosaurus and Rhacheosaurus, both equipped with long, thin snouts specialized for fish and other small prey.
